sprint: Magic Publish — Sprint M8 (Performance & QA). Per docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md: "Goal. Production readiness. Scope. Stress testing, large stories, long books, theme validation, Museum Gallery verification, memory profiling, regression testing. Success criteria. No regression across existing publishing capabilities." Measurement first, then the smallest fix that genuinely solves what the measurement found — deliberately touching neither ReelComposer, publishStudio.js, nor renderer/slideRenderer.js.
task: Measured before assuming. A profiler (m8_profile.mjs) drove the real MAGIC destination's createCanvas/renderPage/encodePage exactly the way PublishStudio._renderNextPage does, for stories of 1/2/4/8/12 pages, sampling resident bitmap bytes right before compose — which is the peak, since finish() flattens every page's frames into one list. Result: memory AND running time were both linear and unbounded in story length — 1 page 12 frames 94.9MB 6.2s film; 2 pages 189.8MB 12.4s; 4 pages 48 frames 379.7MB 24.7s; 8 pages 96 frames 759.4MB 49.4s; 12 pages 144 frames 1139.1MB 74.2s. About 95MB and ~6s of film per page. Root cause: encodePage mints one 1080x1920 off-screen canvas (~7.9MB) per non-finished stage — up to 12 stages/page (blank + world + artwork + decorations + up to 8 word steps) — and every page's frames are simultaneously resident. The 74-second film time was NOT part of the original hypothesis and turned out to be the more product-relevant half: docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md section 5 already declared correct pacing as "~4-6s per page and ~20-25s total for a four-page story, deliberately short so it is rewatched rather than endured" — a 74-second reveal is endured, not rewatched. So the engineering ceiling and the product ceiling are the same fix. THE FIX: a story-wide budget, in two halves, both of which make a long book's reveal BRISKER, never SHORTER — no page is ever dropped. (1) MagicReveal.fitToBudget(stages,maxFrames) samples a page's stages evenly while always keeping the ends (the blank page and the finished page), so a page can be thinned but never removed; storyDestinations' encodePage spends MAGIC_MAX_FRAMES=48 evenly across the story's pages with a MAGIC_MIN_FRAMES_PER_PAGE=2 floor. 48 was chosen so the four-page reference story — the shape section 5 was written around — is completely unaffected: its natural 48 frames is exactly the cap. (2) paceToBudget() in finish() scales holds so the whole reel lands inside MAGIC_TARGET_TOTAL_MS=40000. Narrated pages are deliberately never squeezed — their holds are sized to the child's own voice, and speeding them up would cut a sentence off; a heavily narrated book is allowed to run long, because the voice is the point and the reveal is the frame around it. TWO GENUINE DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY THE SUITE AND FIXED AT ROOT rather than worked around. (a) The floor inflated frames that were already shorter: MAGIC_MIN_HOLD_MS=260 was applied as an absolute floor via Math.max(260, hold*k), but a word step is deliberately WORD_HOLD_MS=140, so pacing pushed those UP to 260 and made the reveal LONGER (a 12-page story landed at 33.6s against a 30s target — arithmetic: keeps indices 0,4,7,11 = 750/140/140/2200 = 3230/page x12 = 38760; k=0.774 gives 581/108/108/1703; the 108s clamp up to 260 = 2804/page x12 = 33648, matching the observed 33636). Fixed by making the floor PER-FRAME — floor: Math.min(MAGIC_MIN_HOLD_MS, hold), so a frame already under it keeps its own length — plus an 8-pass water-filling loop that pins whatever the current rate would push under its own floor and shares what is left among the rest, so a reveal full of already-short word steps still lands ON the budget instead of overshooting it. (b) Transition time was not counted: the old comment claimed that could only make a page "slightly longer... the safe direction", but at 48 frames it is ~10.3s (620 + 11x520 + 12x3x110) plus the card's 2500+620 = 3120 — a third of the budget again, not slight, and the end-to-end check filmed at 53.2s against the 40s target. Fixed by seeding fixedMs with the closing card and adding each frame's own transitionMs(f.transition), READ FROM ReelComposer's own exported TURN_MS/WASH_MS/RISE_MS/DRAW_MS rather than copied, so there is one place to change and no chance of the budget drifting out of step with what actually films. MAGIC_TARGET_TOTAL_MS moved 30000 -> 40000 as a direct consequence: with transitions counted, the four-page reference story's real nominal length is 24720 holds + 11220 transitions + 3120 card = 39060ms, so a 30000 target would have squeezed the very story section 5 was written around; 40000 is that story's own real length, so it stays untouched by definition and everything longer paces back to it (hand-verified: 8-page ~39.4s, 12-page exactly 40.0s, 24-page ~40.5s). FOUR ALTERNATIVES WERE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, recorded so they are not re-litigated: lazy frame rendering (a ~65ms render would stall the real-time rAF recording loop, and is an architecture change to shipped ReelComposer that Story Reel depends on); compressed-blob frames plus async createImageBitmap (genuinely elegant and named as the real long-term answer, deferred); ImageBitmap/GPU-backed storage (still ~8MB of some memory); a fixed per-page allowance (still O(n)). DISCLOSED RESIDUAL, not hidden: the memory ceiling is still ~380MB rather than ~24MB — bounding frames CAPS memory rather than eliminating it. But 380MB was already the shipped four-page footprint, so the fix converts a starting point into a ceiling; the compressed-frame architecture is the real long-term answer and remains deferred, approval-gated work. The STRIP destination (js/magicStrip.js, M5) calls MagicReveal.revealStages itself and was NOT changed, so the Magic Strip is unaffected by the budget. Verified 47/47 via a new magic_m8_verify suite across six sections: fitToBudget's sampling (budget 4 of 12 stages yields k0/k4/k7/k11, ends always kept, strictly increasing indices at every budget 2..12, caller's list never mutated, degenerate budgets 0/1/-5 still keep the finished page); the frame budget holding flat at 48 frames / 379.7MB for 4, 8, 12 AND 24 pages with every page keeping at least 2 frames; pacing (4-page 24.7s untouched, 12-page 26.6s of holds, pacing only ever shortens a frame and a frame that was long enough to squeeze never drops under the floor); Museum Gallery — all three canonical hashes recomputed from the real .vtheme and byte-identical (1f54eb660f7beb53 showcase, 843e68f2cffb3c2e portrait, 969a67e5c984647b quote), with each representation then run through the real Magic pipeline and Quote — which has no Frame pipeline at all — confirmed to still reveal from a blank page; a real 12-page publish end to end producing a 12.3MB video with EBML magic 1a45dfa3 read off the blob's own first four bytes, a nominal reel length of exactly 40.0s (the water-filling lands precisely on budget) filming in 45.6s of wall clock, and every __magicOwned canvas released; and zero page errors. TWO TEST-SIDE UPDATES, both disclosed as intended consequences rather than regressions: C4 became C4a/C4b because the original assertion (every hold >= 260) encoded the pre-fix absolute-floor semantics — the genuine invariants are that pacing may only ever SHORTEN a frame and that a frame naturally >= 260 never drops under it, which required capturing pre-finish holds in the probe; and E4 became E4a/E4b after nominal landed at exactly 40.0s while wall clock measured 45.9s — ~5.4s of real-time recorder slip across ~98 scheduled boundaries, which no budget controls and which varies by machine — so rather than simply moving the goalpost, a pass-through compose tap was added to measure the exact, timing-independent thing the budget actually governs (nominal length, asserted <= 40.0s) with wall clock held to the looser <60s bar the check was always reaching for. Regression: magic_m1 32/32, magic_m2 33/33, magic_m3 32/32, magic_m4 41/41, magic_m5 43/43, magic_m6 35/35, magic_m7 38/38, reel 15/15, reel_backdrop 10/10, reel_pageturn 12/12, voice 16/16, voice_note 22/22, both goldenBuilds PASS.
